newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Fed Gov Angell sees Fed on hold, inflation tame.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Fed Gov Angell sees Fed on hold, inflation tame.

text.p: Former Federal Reserve Board Governor and consummate inflation hawk Wayne Angell said the U.S. central bank will likely keep interest rates steady as inflation is not expected to accelerate.

Speaking to the U.S. cable television network CNBC, Angell said, "I think it would be prudent to raise rates if we get some signal that the Federal Reserve is providing excess liquidity, and that wouldn't show up in the stock market; that would show up in the commodity market ... I'm not looking for that to happen this year."
Angell, chief economist at Bear, Stearns and Co Inc, said the case for a Fed tightening now is not as strong as it was in July of last year.

"In July, they (Fed policymakers) were expecting 2.25 percent growth and we ended up with 3.25 percent growth, and now they're expecting 2.25 percent growth and (they) are suggesting maybe rates should go higher," Angell said.

The Bear, Stearns economist said Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan was "talking tough" earlier Wednesday during the first leg of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins address before Congress, adding that he does not expect the Fed Chairman to hike rates at its next policy confab on March 25.
Angell said commodity prices are "fairly well behaved," and that with no run-up in oil or food prices, the Fed should stand pat on rates.
"... I just do not believe that when they come to the March meeting that they'll be raising rates, so I think he's talking tough because he's not going to act," Angell said.
